checks.name: back-plate-only panel (cantilever from the body; carries the head post)
checks.criterion: plate cantilever under 50 N normal at the far edge < 10 MPa (warn level: the panel lies under the head; load reaches it through the head's back ribs)
checks.proposed_fix: the 2.0 mm plate behind the head is the weakest structural element (est. crack at ~100 N on the top edge; the head post P stands on it).  Raise every Z level by 1.0 (plate 3.0): sigma x (2/3)^2 -> ~17 MPa, depth 19.3 mm; or accept and add an inspection note.

checks.name: head vs frame at (12.1, 33.8), z 3.75-10.75
checks.criterion: exposed gap constant (<= 0.1 variation), always < 2.0, or always >= 12 (SPEC V12)
checks.kind: finger-size opening (>= 4 mm) closes below 2 mm (shear / crush)
checks.proposed_fix: Cheek / roof-lobe jaw: where the roof lobes enter the head's I3 slot the slot back wall closes on the lobe end (gap 0.55 at one bank, several mm at the other) and the slot mouth is reachable from the side.  Make the lobe end inside the slot a circular arc about P (Body2D clipped to r <= R_b about P in both lobe sectors, R_b ~17.5) so RoofSweepInv's back wall becomes the concentric arc R_b + 0.55 (constant gap), let the face outline cross the body outline at ~90 deg (locally radial to P) and round the slot-mouth corners r >= 1.0.  A cheek-only change (Face2D U sector(P, 18.5)) was prototyped and does NOT remove the jaw.

checks.name: wheel vs frame at (-16.7, 1.0), z 13.75-15.75
checks.criterion: exposed gap constant (<= 0.1 variation), always < 2.0, or always >= 12 (SPEC V12)
checks.kind: finger-size opening (>= 4 mm) closes below 2 mm (shear / crush)
checks.proposed_fix: Knob vs paw-lip span ends: the knob (r 6-16, z 13.3-18.3) enters each paw span with a vertical end face -> guillotine from >= 12 mm to 1.0 mm.  Cleanest fix: replace the protruding knob by a recessed finger well (spherical dish D 11 x 2.0 deep at r_k 11; nothing of the wheel above z 13.3) - removes this pinch, the knob-chin squeeze and the knob small-part risk; re-run V4 for the fingertip torque.  Mitigation if the knob stays: lead-in cams at the span ends (lip inner radius 17 -> 22 over the last 15 deg, paw top chamfered 45 deg down to z 13.4) and a documented V12 waiver for the user-driven knob.

checks.name: head vs wheel at (7.3, 20.0), z 12.25-15.25
checks.criterion: exposed gap constant (<= 0.1 variation), always < 2.0, or always >= 12 (SPEC V12)
checks.kind: finger-size opening closes by >= 2 mm to a gap inside the 2-12 mm band (squeeze)
checks.proposed_fix: Cheek / chin vs ball rim + knob crescent: the face's lower edge diverges from the rim, so the gap at fixed points varies 2.5-5.6 mm as the head banks.  Keep the chin-to-rim gap < 2.0 along the whole crescent (FaceUp = Face - (BallEx (+) 0.5) only where the face is within 4 mm of the rim, i.e. a rim-concentric chin) and remove the knob (finger well).

checks.name: head reads as the biggest shape (kawaii: big head, small body)
checks.criterion: face width >= ball diameter
checks.suggestion: grow the face disc to r 17.5 with C_h = P + (0, 12.0) (chin stays put; I_h rises ~30 %, still inside 4-8e-6 - re-run V13/V4), or tint the ball a softer colour so the face dominates

checks.name: ears tall enough to read as cat ears
checks.criterion: ear tips >= 6 mm above the crown (about 0.35-0.5 x head radius)
checks.suggestion: ear tip at C_h + 24.5 (sin 30, cos 30) with base at +-12 / +-50 deg and rounding (+)2.0 (-)0.8; re-check I_h (+~4 %) and the ear root (still >= 8 x 5)

checks.name: head shiver amplitude visible as a giggle
checks.criterion: >= 8 mm peak-to-peak at the ear tips

checks.name: optional colour swap z 15.6-16.2 colours exactly the face features
checks.criterion: only the eyes / nose / mouth change colour
checks.note: the swap also colours the paw tops (frame) and a band of the knob; debossed features (mouth, blush, inner ears) stay face-coloured
checks.suggestion: make the mouth a raised 0.6 x 0.9 line, and drop the paw top to z 15.4 (or start the swap at z 16.05 with 0.7 tall eyes / nose) so the swap catches only the face
